exposure: insulin pump use (at baseline and changes over time)
depressive symptoms (measured by Children's Depression Inventory - CDI)
socio-demographic factors (ethnicity, caregiver education, insurance, caregiver number)
outcome: change in method of insulin delivery (switching from pump to multiple daily injections - MDI)
cohort: The study included 150 adolescents with type 1 diabetes (T1D).
finding: Baseline insulin pump use was associated with lower mean A1c, while switching from pump to multiple daily injections and higher depressive symptoms were linked to increased A1c and a greater likelihood of discontinuing pump use.
